title: Goalkeeper
caption: What a keeper does in a match
b1: The goalkeeper is the only player allowed to handle the ball inside her own penalty area. She wears a different colour so the referee can spot her instantly.
b2: Stopping shots — the most visible part. But the keeper also organises the defence: she sees the whole pitch from behind and uses her voice to tell defenders where to stand. Distribution — once she has the ball, the attack starts in her hands: roll it to a nearby defender, throw it, or kick it long. Reading the space behind — when opponents play the ball over the defence, the keeper comes out and claims it before the striker gets there.
b3: A good keeper often makes no spectacular save at all — she is simply always standing in the right place.
t1: Handling is allowed only inside your own penalty area.
t2: Your voice is the main tool — you organise the defence.
